title: AFP confirms China plane in West Philippine Sea
summary: The Armed Forces of the Philippines yesterday confirmed it has monitored a Chinese H-6 strategic bomber plane over the West Philippine Sea this week.

blocks.text: This file photo shows a Chinese Xian H-6 bomber flying over the sea near Japan in late 2025.
MANILA, Philippines — The Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) yesterday confirmed it has monitored a Chinese H-6 strategic bomber plane over the West Philippine Sea (WPS) this week.
The Chinese plane was observed between Bajo de Masinloc and Luzon, 170 nautical miles away from Metro Manila.

At the Kapihan sa Manila Prince Hotel forum, AFP spokesperson for the West Philippine Sea retired Rear Admiral Roy Vincent Trinidad said the improved surveillance and monitoring capabilities helped in monitoring the aircraft.
He said the aircraft’s presence was not a reason for concern as there is no indication that the aircraft was rehearsing for a missile strike.
“It only shows that the entire PLA (People’s Liberation Army) is now flexing its muscles. Their patrols before were closer to the mainland of China. Today, they almost reach us,” he said.

Meanwhile, the Philippine Coast Guard managed to avoid a dangerous maneuver made by China while authorities repelled two illegally anchored ships off Panata Island, Rear Admiral Jay Tarriela, PCG spokesman for the West Philippine Sea, said on Tuesday.

According to Tarriela, the PCG deployed BRP Cabra and its rigid-hull inflatable boat to drive away Chinese maritime militia vessels, which were anchored about five nautical miles from the Philippine-occupied feature. A China Coast Guard ship was also present in the area during the incident.
Meanwhile, PCG Commandant Admiral Rommel Supangan led the commissioning of three additional vessels into Coast Guard service to further strengthen the organization’s operational capabilities.

PCG spokesperson Commodore Noemie Cayabyab said the BRP Patag, BRP Pag-asa and BRP Kalikasan were put into service yesterday at the National Headquarters in Port Area, Manila, in line with the celebration of Coast Guard Fleet’s 62nd anniversary. — Andrew Ronquillo, Bella Cariaso
